findings.reason: the node's scope names a module that does not exist and omits the one that carries the decode it must make single, so either the node is blocked at its first ledger-level edit or it creates a phantom module beside the real one.
findings.text: §45 grants `reckon/crew/ledger.py`, but the repository has no such file: the module is `reckon/ledger.py`, which holds `load` at :2113, `_index_payload` at :1675 and `_last_good_index_data` at :1749, and the same plan cites `reckon/ledger.py` correctly elsewhere. A worker dispatched on this scope therefore holds a grant for a path that resolves nowhere and no grant for the file that owns both functions its done-when counts (`_index_payload`, `_last_good_index_data`), so a decode-once hook added at the ledger level is a change it is fenced out of — the exact blocked-run shape §41 and §43 exist to remove.

findings.reason: a gate whose target the section's own measurement shows unreachable sends the node at a fix that cannot satisfy it, or invites a threshold that gets quietly relaxed at review time.
findings.text: §45's deliverable is one ledger index decode per batch, but its all_debug arm requires "the head's wall time per entry below half the base's". Its own cited profile puts `ledger.load` at 21 % of 977 s of main-thread samples, with `file_memo.memoized_key` 18 %, plan discovery 8 % and git ancestry 7 % beside it. Caching the decode removes at most 7/8 of that 21 % (the batch holds 8 entries), about 18 points, leaving the head near 0.8 of the base's per-entry time — so the stated gate cannot pass from the stated change, and the rest of the per-entry cost sits in frames the section names but does not put in scope. Either the threshold is a figure the deliverable can reach, or the deliverable has to cover the other named frames; as written a node either fails its own done-when or reports a result the measure was tuned around.
